name: The ground (gzhi) in the Great Perfection

definitions.definition: The primordial state prior to saṃsāra and nirvāṇa: essence primordially pure, nature spontaneously present, compassion all-pervading; neither buddha nor being, it becomes one or the other by recognition or non-recognition of its display.
The ground of the ground-path-fruit scheme: buddha-nature, present in all beings.

relations.note: the ground is the buddha-nature of the sūtras seen from the Atiyoga standpoint
the ground is not the saṃsāric all-base

name: Primordial purity (ka dag)

definitions.definition: The empty essence of the ground, never stained by delusion; the object of cutting through.

name: Spontaneous presence (lhun grub)

definitions.definition: The luminous nature of the ground in which lights, kāyas and qualities are present without effort; brought out in direct crossing.

name: Essence, nature and compassion — the three aspects of the ground

definitions.definition: The ground's three inseparable aspects: empty essence (ngo bo), luminous nature (rang bzhin), all-pervading compassion (thugs rje); the Kunjed Gyalpo's opening chapter already sets out the retinues as coming from 'its own nature, own essence and own compassion'.

name: The youthful vase body (gzhon nu bum sku)

definitions.definition: The ground's luminosity enclosed within like light in a vase, prior to its outward display; its 'breaking open' is the emergence of ground-appearances; the fruit is the return of the ground to itself.

name: The eight gateways of spontaneous presence

definitions.definition: The eight ways in which the ground's display emerges: as compassion, as light, as wisdom, as kāyas, as non-duality, as freedom from extremes, as the gate of pure wisdom and as the gate of impure saṃsāra.

notes: Member list from memory; order uncertain.

name: Ground-appearances and how delusion arises

definitions.definition: When the ground-appearances arise, recognizing them as self-display is liberation; not recognizing them, awareness takes them as other, dualistic grasping arises and the realms unfold — 'one ground, two paths'.
In the Guhyagarbha: from the sugata-essence one's own conceptual karma emanates bodies, abodes and sufferings; grasping I and mine ties knots in space.

name: The three kinds of ignorance (ma rig pa gsum)

definitions.definition: Ignorance of single identity (bdag nyid gcig pu'i ma rig pa), co-emergent ignorance (lhan cig skyes pa'i ma rig pa) and conceptualizing ignorance (kun tu brtags pa'i ma rig pa); the Aspiration of Samantabhadra speaks of a blank unawareness and a conceptual ignorance.

members: bdag nyid gcig pu'i ma rig pa
lhan cig skyes pa'i ma rig pa
kun tu brtags pa'i ma rig pa

name: One ground, two paths, two results

definitions.definition: Saṃsāra and nirvāṇa have one ground; recognition (awareness) and non-recognition (ignorance) are the two paths; buddhahood and saṃsāra the two results.
Recited daily in the Aspiration of Samantabhadra.

name: Samantabhadra's primordial liberation

definitions.definition: Samantabhadra was liberated without effort by recognizing the ground-appearances as his own display, without having done a single virtue; he is the model and the nature of every being's awareness.
Kuntu Zangpo is the Bön-body, primordial buddha of Bön.

name: The all-creating king: bodhicitta as the creator of all

definitions.definition: In the mind series the nature of mind speaks as 'the all-creating king': teacher, teaching, retinue, place and time arise from it; there is no maker apart from it; it is self-arising wisdom beyond cause and condition. It is not a creator deity separate from beings but the nature of mind itself.

relations.note: the Nyingma deny a creator god; the 'all-creator' is awareness

notes: cpt:isvara-creator is referenced as the likely id of a creator-god concept elsewhere; if absent, read the note as the Nyingma's own denial.

name: Awareness (rig pa) and ordinary mind (sems)

definitions.definition: Ordinary mind is dualistic, conceptual, arising from non-recognition; awareness is the non-dual knowing of the ground. Dzogchen practice begins by distinguishing them (ru shan) and then resting in awareness; mistaking sems for rig pa is the principal error.
Bön Dzogchen likewise distinguishes the moving mind from the nature of mind (sems nyid) and awareness.

name: The all-base (kun gzhi) distinguished from the dharmakāya

definitions.definition: Longchenpa distinguishes the all-base — the neutral, unaware ground of karmic traces — from the dharmakāya, and all-base consciousness from wisdom; an indifferent, blank state is the all-base, not awareness.
In Bön the kun gzhi is itself the ultimate base, empty and clear, inseparable from awareness.

relations.note: the same word names different things

name: The Great Perfection (rdzogs pa chen po)

definitions.definition: Everything is already complete in the nature of mind; there is nothing to add by meditation, samaya or path; whatever appears is one in suchness and to be left unaltered.
The unsurpassed way of Bön, the same name for Bön's highest teaching.

name: Non-meditation in the Great Perfection

definitions.definition: 'Whatever is meditated is my sickness': the nature is not produced by meditating; resting without fabrication is not a meditation on an object.

relations.note: the fourth yoga of Mahāmudrā is also called non-meditation

name: Definitive and provisional teaching in the Kunjed Gyalpo

definitions.definition: The Kunjed Gyalpo calls the separate teachings of the three-kāya teachers provisional (drang ba'i lung) with respect to suchness, and the teaching that everything is one in the nature beyond effort definitive.

relations.note: a text-internal use of the neyārtha / nītārtha distinction

name: The four samayas of the Great Perfection

definitions.definition: Non-existence (med pa), evenness / all-pervasiveness (phyal ba), spontaneous presence (lhun grub) and singularity (gcig pu): commitments kept by realization; the Kunjed Gyalpo speaks of 'samaya with nothing to guard'.

name: The four ways of leaving as it is (cog bzhag bzhi)

definitions.definition: View like a mountain, meditation like an ocean, conduct as appearances, fruit as awareness — each 'left as it is'.

name: Garab Dorje's three statements that hit the vital point

definitions.definition: Introduce directly to one's own nature; decide on one thing; gain confidence in liberation — the whole path of cutting through in three lines.

name: The modes of liberation (grol lugs)

definitions.definition: Primordial liberation (ye grol), self-liberation (rang grol), liberation upon arising (shar grol), naked liberation (cer grol) and liberation from extremes (mtha' grol); thoughts are said to be freed like meeting an old friend, like a snake uncoiling its knot, or like a thief in an empty house.

name: The three series of Dzogchen (sde gsum)

definitions.definition: Mañjuśrīmitra divided the Dzogchen teachings into the mind series (sems sde), the space series (klong sde) and the instruction series (man ngag sde).

name: The four cycles of the instruction series

definitions.definition: Śrī Siṃha divided the instruction series into the outer, inner, secret and innermost secret unsurpassed cycles; the last is the Heart-essence (snying thig).

members: innermost secret unsurpassed (yang gsang bla na med pa)

name: The four visions of direct crossing (snang ba bzhi)

definitions.definition: Direct perception of dharmatā; increase of experience; awareness reaching its full measure; exhaustion of phenomena in dharmatā — the stages of direct crossing (restricted practice; only the doctrine is recorded).

relations.note: the final vision can issue in the rainbow body

notes: The path map pth:dzogchen-four-visions is owned by U51.

name: The lamps (sgron ma) of the instruction series

definitions.definition: Four lamps: the far-reaching water lamp (the eyes), the lamp of the empty sphere, the lamp of the pure expanse, and the lamp of self-arising wisdom; six when the lamp of the flesh heart and of the smooth white channel are added. Doctrinal anatomy; their use belongs to the restricted direct crossing.

members: thig le stong pa'i sgron ma
dbyings rnam par dag pa'i sgron ma
shes rab rang byung gi sgron ma

name: The abode of wisdom in the body (Heart-essence anatomy)

definitions.definition: Wisdom dwells in the heart (tsitta palace) as the youthful vase body; the peaceful deities in the heart and the wrathful in the skull; the crystal kati channel connects heart and eyes, through which the lamps manifest.

relations.note: Dzogchen's anatomy of wisdom differs from the completion stage's channels, winds and drops

name: Channels, winds and essences in Anuyoga

definitions.definition: The completion-stage body of three channels (central, right, left), the wheels, the winds that move in them and the essences (thig le); worked with in Anuyoga to bring the winds into the central channel and give rise to bliss-emptiness.

name: The rainbow body ('ja' lus)

definitions.definition: The fruit of direct crossing and sometimes of cutting through: at death the body shrinks and dissolves into light leaving hair and nails, accompanied by rainbows and lights; the great transference body departs without death.
The Zhang Zhung Nyengyü counts twenty-four masters who attained the rainbow body; Shardza Tashi Gyaltsen (1934) in recent memory.

name: Post-death meditation (thugs dam)

definitions.definition: After the outer breath stops, an accomplished practitioner rests in the clear light of death for days, the body upright or lifelike and warm at the heart, before the consciousness departs.

name: The nine vehicles (theg pa rim pa dgu)

definitions.definition: Śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha and bodhisattva (the vehicles leading from the origin of suffering); kriyā, ubhaya and yoga (the vehicles of Vedic austerity, outer tantras); mahāyoga, anuyoga and atiyoga (the vehicles of overpowering means, inner tantras). Each is complete for its practitioners; the higher include the lower.
The Kunjed Gyalpo's nine passes, scriptures and paths lead to the single vehicle of the all-creator, which is reached without travelling.

relations.note: both traditions order their teaching in nine vehicles; the contents differ

name: The eighteen great Mahāyoga tantras (tantra section)

definitions.definition: The tantra section of Mahāyoga: five root tantras of body, speech, mind, qualities and activity (Sangs rgyas mnyam sbyor, Zla gsang thig le, Gsang ba 'dus pa, Dpal mchog dang po, Karma mā le), five practice tantras, five activity tantras and two supplementary tantras (the Rnam snang sgyu 'phrul drva ba and the Noose of Method), with the Guhyagarbha as their summary root.

notes: Members recalled from memory; the practice and activity tantras not listed (gap). Noose of Method and several root tantras are extant in the local Derge Kangyur (Tōh 835; 366-367; 477; 487-488).

name: The Eight Herukas / Eight Pronouncements (bka' brgyad)

definitions.definition: The sādhana section of Mahāyoga: five transcendent (Mañjuśrī-Yamāntaka body, Hayagrīva speech, Yangdag mind, Chemchok-Amṛta qualities, Vajrakīla activity) and three mundane (Mamo, Jigten Chötö, Möpa Drakngak) heruka practices, entrusted to eight Indian vidyādharas and given by Padmasambhava to his disciples.

name: The eight vidyādharas of the Kagye transmission

definitions.definition: The eight Indian masters to whom the ḍākinī entrusted the eight heruka tantras: Mañjuśrīmitra (body), Nāgārjuna (speech), Hūṃkara (mind), Vimalamitra (qualities), Prabhahasti (activity), Dhanasaṃskṛta (Mamo), Rambuguhya-Devacandra (worldly offering) and Śāntigarbha (wrathful mantra).

notes: Assignment of masters to classes from memory.

name: Mahāyoga, Anuyoga and Atiyoga as generation, completion and great perfection

definitions.definition: Mahāyoga emphasizes the generation stage and the view of purity and equality; Anuyoga the completion stage and the union of expanse and wisdom; Atiyoga awareness beyond both. The Garland of Views ranks them.

name: The three samādhis of Mahāyoga generation

definitions.definition: Every Mahāyoga sādhana begins from the samādhi of suchness (emptiness), the all-illuminating samādhi (compassion) and the causal samādhi (the seed syllable), from which the maṇḍala is generated.

members: de bzhin nyid kyi ting nge 'dzin
kun tu snang ba'i ting nge 'dzin

name: Great purity and equality (dag mnyam chen po)

definitions.definition: All phenomena are primordially pure as deities and pure lands and equal as emptiness; purity and equality are inseparable (the 'superior two truths' of Mahāyoga). The Guhyagarbha shows the aggregates as the buddhas and all as unborn in being born.

relations.note: the Mahāyoga 'superior' two truths add purity of appearance to the sūtra two truths

name: The five kāyas

definitions.definition: Dharmakāya, sambhogakāya, nirmāṇakāya, with the unchanging vajrakāya and the fully enlightened (abhisambodhi) kāya; the Guhyagarbha says the five kāyas are spontaneously perfected.

relations.note: an expanded form of the trikāya

name: The three bodies of a buddha

definitions.definition: Dharmakāya (Samantabhadra), sambhogakāya (the five families in Akaniṣṭha), nirmāṇakāya (Garab Dorje, Śākyamuni, Padmasambhava, the six sages); in the Kunjed Gyalpo the retinues of nature, essence and compassion.
Bön-body (Kuntu Zangpo), body of perfection (Shenlha Ökar), emanation body (Tönpa Shenrab).

name: Buddha-nature (tathāgatagarbha, buddhadhātu)

definitions.definition: For the Nyingma (Mipham), the sugata-essence is the union of luminosity and emptiness with the qualities spontaneously present, neither a mere absence nor a self; the Guhyagarbha makes it the source from which beings' conceptual karma emanates the realms.

name: The Nyingma view of buddha-nature (Mipham)

definitions.definition: Buddha-nature is luminosity-emptiness; it is not established as a self, nor is it a mere non-affirming negation; the qualities are present from the beginning, which is why the ground can be called primordially enlightened.

name: Enumerated and non-enumerated ultimate (Mipham)

definitions.definition: The enumerated (rnam grangs pa) ultimate is emptiness as the negation of true existence, an object of reasoning; the non-enumerated (rnam grangs ma yin pa) ultimate is the union beyond the four extremes, realized in meditative equipoise.

name: The four valid cognitions (Mipham)

definitions.definition: Two valid cognitions of the ultimate (of the enumerated and the non-enumerated ultimate) and two of the conventional (of limited, impure vision and of pure vision); pure-vision valid cognition establishes the purity of appearances taught in the tantras.

name: The three lineages: kama, terma and pure vision

definitions.definition: The long lineage of the spoken word (ring brgyud bka' ma), the short lineage of treasures (nye brgyud gter ma) and the profound lineage of pure visions (zab mo dag snang).

name: The three and the six transmissions

definitions.definition: All teachings pass by the mind-transmission of the victors, the symbolic transmission of the vidyādharas and the oral transmission of persons; treasures add prophetic authorization, empowerment through aspiration and entrustment to the ḍākinīs.

name: How treasures are concealed and revealed

definitions.definition: Padmasambhava teaches a disciple, seals the teaching in the disciple's mind by aspiration and empowerment, has it written in symbolic script and hidden (in the earth or the mind) under a protector; at the prophesied time the disciple's rebirth, the revealer, finds the sign, decodes it and establishes the teaching, often after years of secrecy.
Bön treasures were hidden during the persecutions and recovered by revealers such as Shenchen Luga.

name: Secrecy and the fit vessel

definitions.definition: The Great Perfection is kept secret from those without fortune, who are to practise the vehicles of cause and result; the teacher examines the student and gives the essence only to those bearing the signs.
The Guhyagarbha's secret instruction is given only to trained, fit vessels; proclaimed to the deluded it brings ruin to both.

name: Teacher and disciple in the Nyingma

definitions.definition: The teacher is examined first (pure vows, learning, compassion, experience, freedom from worldly aims), then followed with faith and service and emulated; devotion is the key to the blessing; the disciple too is tested for signs and faith.

name: The four empowerments

definitions.definition: Vase, secret, wisdom-knowledge and word (or precious) empowerments, purifying body, speech, mind and all three and planting the seeds of the four kāyas; received from the guru in guru yoga.

members: shes rab ye shes kyi dbang

name: Samaya in the Nyingma tantras

definitions.definition: The commitments of body, speech and mind binding disciple, teacher and deity: kept, they bring accomplishment and great wonder; broken, they ruin the breaker; restored through confession and feast offering.

name: The three roots (rtsa ba gsum)

definitions.definition: Guru, yidam and ḍākinī (or protector): the inner refuge and the roots of blessing, accomplishment and activity.

name: The four thoughts that turn the mind (blo ldog rnam bzhi)

definitions.definition: Contemplation of the precious human birth, of impermanence and death, of the defects of saṃsāra and of karma, which turn the mind from worldly life to the Dharma; the first part of the preliminaries.

name: The eight freedoms and ten advantages (dal 'byor)

definitions.definition: A precious human life is free of the eight unfree states (hells, hungry spirits, animals, long-lived gods, barbarians, those with wrong views, where no buddha has come, those with impaired faculties) and has ten advantages, five personal and five circumstantial.

name: The four powers of confession

definitions.definition: Support (refuge and bodhicitta before Vajrasattva), regret, resolution not to repeat, and the antidote (practice, mantra) — the purification in Vajrasattva practice.

members: gnyen po kun tu spyod pa'i stobs

name: The three excellences (dam pa gsum)

definitions.definition: Every practice should begin with bodhicitta, be carried out without conceptual reference and end with dedication of merit.

members: sbyor ba sems bskyed dam pa
dngos gzhi dmigs med dam pa

name: Understanding, experience and realization (go myong rtogs)

definitions.definition: Intellectual understanding (go ba) is like a patch that falls off, experience (myong ba) like mist that fades, realization (rtogs pa) is unchanging; meditative experiences are not to be mistaken for realization.

name: The experiences of bliss, clarity and non-thought

definitions.definition: Signs of meditation that arise naturally; attached to, bliss leads to the desire realm, clarity to the form realm and non-thought to the formless realm; released without clinging they support realization.

name: The six intermediate states (bar do drug)

definitions.definition: The bardos of life (skye gnas), dream (rmi lam), meditation (bsam gtan), dying ('chi kha), dharmatā (chos nyid) and becoming (srid pa); the Heart-essence also counts four (life, dying, dharmatā, becoming).

name: The dissolution of the elements at death

definitions.definition: At death earth dissolves into water, water into fire, fire into wind, wind into consciousness, with outer and inner signs; then the white appearance, the red increase and the black near-attainment, after which the ground luminosity dawns.

name: Mother and child luminosity

definitions.definition: The ground luminosity that dawns for every being at death (mother) meets the luminosity recognized in practice (child); for the practitioner who recognizes it the meeting is liberation in the dharmakāya.
The Bön teaching of mother and son clear light at death.

name: The hundred peaceful and wrathful deities

definitions.definition: Forty-two peaceful deities (Samantabhadra and Samantabhadrī, the five buddhas with consorts, eight male and eight female bodhisattvas, six sages, four male and four female gatekeepers) and fifty-eight wrathful (five herukas with consorts, eight gaurīs, eight piśācīs, four gatekeepers, twenty-eight īśvarīs), present in the body and appearing in the bardo of dharmatā.

name: The bardo of becoming (srid pa'i bar do)

definitions.definition: A mental body driven by karma wanders, sees the judgement of the Lord of Death and is drawn to a womb; the instructions teach closing the womb door or choosing a birth.

name: Signs of death and their reversal

definitions.definition: Outer, inner and secret signs of approaching death are examined; untimely death can be averted by ransom and longevity rites; when death is certain, one prepares with transference and the bardo instructions.

name: The Copper-Coloured Mountain (zangs mdog dpal ri)

definitions.definition: Padmasambhava's pure land on the rākṣasa island of Cāmara, where he dwells in his palace of Lotus Light; aspired to as a place of rebirth.

name: The eight manifestations of Padmasambhava (gu ru mtshan brgyad)

definitions.definition: Tsokye Dorje (lake-born vajra), Padmasambhava, Loden Chokse, Padma Gyalpo, Nyima Özer, Shākya Senge, Senge Dradrok and Dorje Drolö — forms taken in different episodes of his life.

name: The abbot, the master and the king (mkhan slob chos gsum)

definitions.definition: Śāntarakṣita, Padmasambhava and Trisong Detsen, the three founders of Buddhism at Samye.

name: The twenty-five disciples (rje 'bangs nyer lnga)

definitions.definition: The king and subjects who were Padmasambhava's closest disciples, among them Trisong Detsen, Yeshe Tsogyal, Vairocana, Nupchen Sangye Yeshe, Namkhai Nyingpo and Nyak Jñānakumāra.

notes: Full list varies and is not given (gap).

name: The early and later diffusions (snga dar, phyi dar)

definitions.definition: The Nyingma are the school of the early translations (snga 'gyur) of the imperial period; the later translations (gsar ma) from the late 10th c. founded the Kadam, Sakya, Kagyu and others.

name: The white-robed, long-haired community (gos dkar lcang lo'i sde)

definitions.definition: The lay tantric sangha of the Nyingma, householders keeping tantric vows beside the monastic sangha, with hereditary family lineages.

name: The six mother monasteries of the Nyingma

definitions.definition: Katok, Dorje Drak, Mindroling, Palyul, Dzogchen and Shechen, the principal Nyingma seats and their traditions.

notes: Founding dates from memory; Dorje Drak and Shechen not dated here.

name: The nine ways of Bön (theg pa rim dgu)

definitions.definition: Four causal ways (phywa gshen: prediction and diagnosis; snang gshen: rites for the gods of the visible world; 'phrul gshen: magical rites against harm; srid gshen: funerary rites) and five fruitional ways (dge bsnyen: lay virtue; drang srong: monastic ascetics; a dkar: tantra of the white A; ye gshen: higher tantra; bla med: the Great Perfection).

notes: Optional (Bön). The list follows the Southern Treasure scheme of the Zijid.

name: The four portals and the fifth, the treasury (sgo bzhi mdzod lnga)

definitions.definition: An alternative ordering of Bön: the White Waters (wrathful mantra), Black Waters (magic, rituals, funerals), the Land of Phan (monastic and sūtra teaching), the Master's Guidance (Dzogchen), and the fifth, the treasury comprising all.

name: The four transcendent lords of Bön (bde gshegs gtso bo rnam bzhi)

definitions.definition: Satrig Ersang (the mother of wisdom), Shenlha Ökar (the god of compassion / body of perfection), Sangpo Bumtri (the father, creator of existence) and Tönpa Shenrab (the teacher).

name: The base of all and awareness in Bön Dzogchen

definitions.definition: The base (kun gzhi) is empty and clear; awareness (rig pa) is its knowing; their inseparability (dbyer med) is the natural state; not recognizing it the moving mind arises.

relations.note: functionally the ground of Nyingma Dzogchen

name: Ölmo Lungring and Tagzig

definitions.definition: The land of Tönpa Shenrab's birth in Tagzig, with the nine-storeyed Yungdrung mountain at its centre, from which Bön spread to Zhang Zhung and Tibet.

name: Buddhist historians' three phases of Bön

definitions.definition: Some Buddhist historians (e.g. Thuken's Crystal Mirror) describe Bön in three phases: 'revealed' (brdol bon), 'deviant' ('khyar bon) and 'transformed' (bsgyur bon, borrowing Buddhist texts).
The Bön tradition rejects this schema as a polemical account.

notes: Recorded as the opponents' account (reported by Buddhist historians); see dsp:bon-and-buddhism.
